topicTitle: REST API Development with Spring Boot

lessons.title: REST API Fundamentals and HTTP Methods
lessons.description: Understand REST principles, HTTP requests, responses, status codes and resource-oriented API design.
lessons.content:
REST stands for Representational State Transfer. It is an architectural style commonly used to design web APIs.

A REST API exposes resources through URLs and uses HTTP methods to perform operations. For example, /api/students represents a collection of students, while /api/students/10 represents an individual student.

Common HTTP methods:
GET retrieves a resource.
POST submits data, often to create a resource.
PUT replaces the representation of a resource.
PATCH applies partial modifications.
DELETE removes a resource.

Important HTTP status codes:
200 OK: request succeeded.
201 Created: resource created successfully.
204 No Content: successful response without a body.
400 Bad Request: invalid client request.
401 Unauthorized: authentication is required or invalid.
403 Forbidden: authenticated client lacks permission.
404 Not Found: requested resource does not exist.
409 Conflict: request conflicts with current resource state.
500 Internal Server Error: unexpected server failure.

REST emphasizes stateless requests, a uniform interface, cacheability where appropriate and separation between clients and servers.

JSON is a common response format. HTTP itself does not require REST APIs to use JSON.

Good endpoint names describe resources rather than actions. Prefer GET /api/students/10 instead of GET /api/getStudentById/10.

API design should also consider pagination, filtering, validation, security and consistent error responses.

lessons.title: Request Bodies, DTOs and Validation
lessons.description: Accept JSON input, use DTOs and validate incoming API data.
lessons.content:
A Data Transfer Object, or DTO, represents data exchanged between API clients and the server.

DTOs help avoid exposing persistence entities directly and allow request and response structures to evolve independently.

@RequestBody converts incoming JSON into a Java object using the configured HTTP message converters.

Bean Validation supports annotations such as @NotBlank, @NotNull, @Email, @Size, @Min and @Max.

In a Spring Boot application, validation commonly requires the spring-boot-starter-validation dependency.

@Valid triggers validation of an annotated request body when the appropriate validation provider is configured.

Invalid request bodies commonly produce HTTP 400 responses. Applications can customize the error format using exception handling.

Use clear validation messages and never trust incoming client data.

Validation is different from authorization. A valid request may still be forbidden if the caller lacks permission.

Do not expose passwords, access tokens or other sensitive values in API responses.

lessons.title: Service Layer, CRUD Operations and Spring Data JPA
lessons.description: Separate controller, service and repository responsibilities while implementing CRUD APIs.
lessons.content:
CRUD means Create, Read, Update and Delete.

A maintainable Spring Boot application commonly separates responsibilities into controller, service, repository, entity and DTO layers.

Controller: accepts HTTP requests and creates HTTP responses.
Service: implements business rules and coordinates application operations.
Repository: performs persistence operations.
Entity: maps application data to database tables when using JPA.
DTO: defines the information accepted or returned by an API.

Spring Data JPA provides repository interfaces such as JpaRepository<Entity, ID>.

Common repository methods include save(), findById(), findAll(), existsById() and deleteById().

An entity typically uses @Entity and @Id. Generated primary keys may use @GeneratedValue.

A service can use Optional.orElseThrow() to handle missing records explicitly.

For update operations, first load the existing record, modify permitted fields and persist the result.

Database configuration and a supported JDBC driver are required for a real JPA-backed application.

Use @Transactional when operations need a consistent transaction boundary, particularly when multiple related writes must succeed or fail together.

Do not assume that every delete request succeeds: missing resources and business constraints require deliberate handling.

lessons.title: Exception Handling, API Testing and Best Practices
lessons.description: Build consistent error responses and test REST endpoints effectively.
lessons.content:
Production APIs should return clear and consistent HTTP responses for successful and failed requests.

@RestControllerAdvice defines exception handlers that can apply across multiple REST controllers.

@ExceptionHandler identifies which exception type a handler processes.

ResponseEntity can set appropriate HTTP statuses for errors.

A missing resource should generally produce 404 Not Found rather than an unexpected 500 Internal Server Error.

Do not reveal stack traces, database credentials or internal implementation details in public error messages.

Spring Boot APIs can be tested using tools such as curl, HTTP client applications and automated tests.

MockMvc supports controller-level HTTP request testing without starting a real network server.

Integration tests can verify controllers, services, repositories and database interactions together.

Useful API design practices include versioning where appropriate, pagination for large collections, clear DTOs, input validation, logging, authentication, authorization and rate limiting when needed.

CORS determines which browser origins are allowed to access API responses. It is not a substitute for authentication or authorization.

For a placement platform, a REST API might manage student profiles, assessments, applications and learning progress. Each endpoint should enforce the appropriate access rules.

quizzes.question: Which HTTP method is primarily used to retrieve a resource?
quizzes.explanation: GET requests retrieve representations of resources and should not intentionally modify server state.

quizzes.question: Which Spring annotation is commonly used to create REST controllers?
quizzes.explanation: @RestController combines controller functionality with response-body handling.

quizzes.question: Which annotation reads an ID from a URL such as /api/students/25?
quizzes.explanation: @PathVariable binds a URI template variable to a method parameter.

quizzes.question: Which HTTP status code normally indicates that a resource was created successfully?
quizzes.explanation: 201 Created indicates that a request successfully resulted in creation of a resource.

quizzes.question: What is the main purpose of @RequestBody in Spring MVC?
options: Convert an HTTP request body into a Java object
quizzes.explanation: @RequestBody binds the incoming request body to a method argument through an HTTP message converter.

quizzes.question: Which dependency commonly provides Bean Validation support in Spring Boot?
quizzes.explanation: spring-boot-starter-validation provides the commonly used Bean Validation integration.

quizzes.question: Which Spring Data JPA interface provides common CRUD and pagination methods?
quizzes.explanation: JpaRepository provides persistence operations including save, findById, findAll and delete.

quizzes.question: Which annotation is commonly used to handle exceptions across multiple REST controllers?
quizzes.explanation: @RestControllerAdvice allows shared exception handlers for REST controllers.

quizzes.question: What is the most appropriate response when a requested student record does not exist?
options: Always return 200 with an empty string
quizzes.explanation: 404 Not Found communicates that the requested resource could not be found.

quizzes.question: Which statement about CORS is correct?
options: CORS controls browser access across origins but does not replace authorization
quizzes.explanation: CORS is a browser-enforced cross-origin access mechanism. APIs still need authentication and authorization.

exercises.title: Create Your First Student REST Controller
exercises.description: Implement simple GET endpoints with Spring Boot.
exercises.instructions: Create a Spring Boot application with spring-boot-starter-web. Implement GET /api/students returning a sample list of student names and GET /api/students/{id} returning the requested ID. Use @RestController, @RequestMapping, @GetMapping and @PathVariable. Test both endpoints.

exercises.title: Implement a Validated Student Registration Endpoint
exercises.description: Accept and validate JSON input using DTOs.
exercises.instructions: Create POST /api/students accepting name, email and age in a request DTO. Apply @NotBlank to name, @Email and @NotBlank to email, and @Min(18) to age. Use @Valid and return HTTP 201 for valid requests. Verify that invalid requests return HTTP 400.

exercises.title: Build a Complete Student CRUD REST API
exercises.description: Implement create, read, update and delete endpoints.
exercises.instructions: Build a Student entity with id, name, email and course. Use Spring Data JPA with a configured database. Create controller, service and repository layers. Implement POST /api/students, GET /api/students, GET /api/students/{id}, PUT /api/students/{id} and DELETE /api/students/{id}. Return appropriate HTTP status codes and handle missing IDs.

exercises.title: Debug Incorrect HTTP Responses
exercises.description: Identify REST endpoint design and error-handling problems.
exercises.instructions: A controller uses @GetMapping to delete a student, returns 200 for missing records and exposes raw exception stack traces to clients. Identify all three problems. Rewrite the endpoint using @DeleteMapping, return 404 for missing students and implement safe structured error handling.

exercises.title: Test a REST API with MockMvc
exercises.description: Write automated tests for success and validation failures.
exercises.instructions: Create automated MockMvc tests for a student registration endpoint. Verify that a valid JSON request returns 201, a blank name returns 400 and an invalid email returns 400. Add a test confirming that GET /api/students/{id} returns 404 when the student does not exist.
